David Moyes played an important role in Mikel Arteta's development as a footballer, having given the Spaniard his first opportunity to play in the Premier League during their time together at Everton. Arteta later worked under Arsene Wenger at Arsenal, gaining valuable experience from another highly respected figure in the game.
 The former midfielder eventually returned to Arsenal as manager after Wenger had left the club. Since taking charge, Arteta has developed his own coaching philosophy, with many observers believing that Wenger and Pep Guardiola have had the strongest influence on his approach to management.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement However, Arteta's development has not been shaped by those two coaches alone. His experience under Moyes also appears to have influenced his understanding of leadership, player management and the importance of establishing high standards within a team.
 Arteta prepares for reunion with Moyes
 Arteta will come up against his former manager when Arsenal face Everton , with the Gunners hoping to secure a positive result. However, Moyes is unlikely to make the contest straightforward, as his teams are often difficult to overcome and capable of making life uncomfortable for their opponents.
 Arsenal will need to deliver a strong performance to claim victory, particularly against an Everton side determined to compete. The fixture also provides an opportunity to reflect on the relationship between the two managers and the lessons Arteta may have carried into his own coaching career.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Although Guardiola has played a significant role in shaping Arteta's tactical ideas, Moyes believes there are other important aspects of management that the Arsenal boss could have learned during their time together at Everton.
 (Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)
 Moyes discusses his influence on Arteta
 The Everton manager has admitted that he is unsure how much of his own coaching philosophy Arteta has adopted, especially given the Spaniard's experience working alongside Guardiola. Nevertheless, Moyes hopes that some of his principles have stayed with his former player.
 Speaking via Liverpool Echo , Moyes reflected on the different lessons Arteta may have taken from the managers he worked with throughout his career.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I always look and I think: 'Mikel has had Pep, what would he take from me?' I don't really know. But I think he might take from me a little bit of the other side.
 "I know how Pep works, how good his teams are and what he's seen. He's worked under Pep and he's seen an awful lot of stuff there.
 "But there's a lot of other stuff like having a winning culture and a winning team, how you're dealing with the players, what you're demanding of them, the standards you set. I hope that in some way he might have taken bits of that."
 While Guardiola may have influenced Arteta's tactical approach, the Everton boss believes his emphasis on standards, winning mentality and relationships with players could also have left a lasting impression.
